maya: heads-up — started seeing a slow, tenant-specific increase in KV memory residency on a few noisy tenants over long-context traces. looks like steady growth across ~30m windows, not a single spike.

kv-monitor-bot: alert: kv_residency_percent(tenant=acct-42) > 85% for 00:35:12 — recent snapshots: https://incidents.internal/redwood/1863456789

sanford: ugh. any idea if this correlates with the kernel selector change last night? did we flip any alignment/alloc flags?

oliver: we did push a kernel-selection tweak in the canary — preference for the 'matm' kernel when seq_len>1024 to reduce per-token cycles. diff: `runtime/kernel_selector: prefer_matm_when_longctx=true`

li: repro harness ran a long-context workload and i grabbed a quick perf sample. small excerpt:
```
# perf top (30s)
cpu 0: memcpy: 34.2%\nmm/page_walk: 12.1%\nkv::page_allocate: 9.8%\nkv::evict_scan: 7.6%\n```
Ran `./tools/replay_ctx.sh --tenant acct-42 --seed 7 --len 4500`

maya: interesting — my hypothesis is the MATM path increases contiguous chunk allocations which fragments the slab buckets we use for small KV entries. fragmentation -> more page allocations -> eviction of hot small entries. explains slow growth rather than bursty behavior.

sanford: makes sense. fragmentation would cause live set to appear larger even though active keys stable. can we quantify by bucket-utilization and free-run fragmentation metric?

oliver: i can run a canary toggling selector back and also try increasing the shard-local per-tenant min-residency to force stricter isolation. i worry about latency regressions if we over-allocate.

li: quick experiment idea: flip `prefer_matm=false` + adjust batching heuristic to batch slightly larger (batch_size_target += 16) so we amortize pagewalks. that should reduce overall page pressure at the cost of tail latency for tiny requests.

maya: agreed on experiment matrix. steps: 1) canary selector toggle on one hostpool; 2) enable per-tenant soft-residency cap at 75% for that pool; 3) run replay harness and collect `kv_eviction_count`, `kv_residency_p95`, `kv_fragmentation_ratio`, `token_latency_p99`. post results here. i'll also add an eval prompt set to detect quality regressions.

oliver: i'll provision the canary and kick off the runs in ~10m. tagging @sanford for the metrics dashboard changes.

kv-monitor-bot: snapshot saved: /s3/kv-snapshots/1863456789/snapshot-1.tar.gz — metrics: kv_eviction_count=412, kv_residency_p95=79.3, kv_fragmentation_ratio=0.28. alert cleared.

maya: perfect — thanks. if we see eviction_count drop and fragmentation_ratio improve on canary, we can roll a mitigation (selector revert + tuned batching) while we investigate a long-term fix (slab allocator tweak or per-tenant compaction). :thumbsup:
